sections.h2: Compare pet products and deals without the guesswork
sections.html:
Pet prices vary a lot between online pet stores, supermarkets, subscription brands, independent pet shops and vet practices. The cheapest-looking deal isn’t always the best value, so our guides show you how to compare properly:

  • Food: compare the cost per day at your pet’s feeding amount, not the price per bag or tin.
  • Insurance: compare the type of cover, limits and excess before the premium.
  • Health care: flea, tick and worm treatments can cost less with a written prescription or a vet health plan.
  • Everyday kit: buy beds, crates and harnesses that fit your pet now and later, so you only buy once.

Some things are best done locally. Our local pet services guide explains what to look for in a dog groomer, a dog walker or pet sitter, and boarding kennels and catteries: licences, insurance, qualifications and the questions to ask on a first visit.

Run a pet business? We’re building a list of recommended local suppliers. Get in touch to be considered.

PetSavings is free to use. Some links on the site may be affiliate links: if you buy through them, the retailer or insurer may pay us a commission. It never changes the price you pay, and it doesn’t decide what we write. Read how we make money.

faqs.a: Yes. Our guides are free. When you buy, you deal directly with the retailer, insurer or local business and agree their terms.

faqs.q: Do you sell pet food or insurance?
faqs.a: No. PetSavings is an independent guide and comparison site. We don’t sell products, arrange insurance or give veterinary advice.

faqs.q: Do you cover the US, UK and Europe?
faqs.a: Yes. We explain where rules differ, such as pet food labelling, insurance regulation, prescriptions and licensing for kennels and home boarders.
